risk_if_not_implemented: Without Third-Party Transition Planning, transition activities, responsibilities and timelines are undefined at the point of cessation, so hand-off tasks are missed, ownership is disputed and service continuity suffers. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unperformed / Unowned Control Responsibilities (R-GV-3), Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-5), Third-Party Dependency Failure (R-SC-6), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Supplier Financial Distress / Insolvency (MT-24).

compensating_control_1.name: Responsible, Accountable, Supportive, Consulted & Informed (RASCI) Matrix
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to document and maintain a Responsible, Accountable, Supportive, Consulted & Informed (RASCI) matrix, or similar documentation, to delineate assignment for security, compliance and resilience controls between internal stakeholders and External Service Providers (ESPs).
compensating_control_1.justification: Responsible, Accountable, Supportive, Consulted & Informed (RASCI) Matrix (TPM-11) compensates for the absence of Third-Party Transition Planning (TPM-24.1) by documenting a Responsible, Accountable, Supportive, Consulted & Informed (RASCI) matrix for third-party controls, which establishes the ownership that a transition plan would otherwise assign. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) Plans
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist for process owners to establish and maintain formal Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) plans to ensure information is detailed enough, accurate and representative of current operations in order to sustain and/or restore operations under adverse conditions.
compensating_control_2.justification: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) Plans (BCD-04) compensates for the absence of Third-Party Transition Planning (TPM-24.1) by maintaining Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) plans that already describe how critical services are sustained during disruption, which can be invoked to structure an otherwise unplanned provider transition. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
